title: Stop using Excel for backtesting. Here is a simple Python framework to analyze price action
author: Algo_Architect_FX
selftext:
Hey guys, Algo\_Architect\_FX here.

I see a ton of manual traders in this sub trying to validate their strategies by scrolling back through charts manually or trying to hardcode hundreds of conditional rows into Excel. It’s slow, prone to human error, and completely misses critical data points like volume moving averages or multi-day consecutive trends.

You don't need a degree in Computer Science to build a basic structural screener. If you want to check for highly specific setups—like identifying when an asset has had 6 consecutive lower daily closes combined with a 50% spike above its 200-day average volume—Python can do it in under 30 lines of code.

I’ve put together a completely clean, zero-hype template using the free `yfinance` library that you can run directly inside your browser using Google Colab (no installation required). It covers:

* Automated historical data retrieval
* Basic moving average calculations
* Exact sequential logic testing (e.g., tracking consecutive daily drops without look-ahead bias)

If you're tired of guessing or relying on lagging visual indicators on your charts, drop a comment below with the specific technical setup you're trying to test, and I'll help you map out the logic for it. Let's build better systems.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: worth adding to the template: yfinance auto adjusts by default, so old closes get rewritten for splits and dividends. fine for returns, but any rule keyed on a price level or "close above X" is testing prices that never printed. and the ticker list is today's, so anything delisted just isn't in the test.
